besluite.fout: The preposition 'after' is written without the accent here while the same lesson writes 'Ná die ete'.
besluite.rede: A spelling fix that makes the lesson consistent with itself, with no change in meaning.

besluite.fout: 'Na iemand genoem word' is the looser form and can also be read as 'be called'.
besluite.rede: 'Vernoem' is the exact Afrikaans verb for naming a child after someone, and the meaning stays the same.
'Gaan stry' with 'vandag' reads naturally as Mila's own fear in the story, and 'sou stry' adds a conditional colour while making the narrator's voice stiffer.
'Die baba hoog gehou' is natural Afrikaans, and 'opgehou' could make a Grade 6 reader stumble on 'ophou' meaning 'stop'.

besluite.fout: There is no AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
besluite.rede: 'Haar naam was Zanele' and 'sy was oom Sipho se niggie' are two full clauses, so the AWS 2017 calls for the comma.

besluite.fout: Closing and reopening the quotation with no speaker in between signals a new, unnamed speaker.
besluite.rede: Only Zanele is speaking to Mila here, so one quotation fixes the stumble, and the protected wording stays intact word for word.
'Bekommerd gevoel' is ordinary, natural Afrikaans rather than an anglicism, so swapping it is a lateral move in the author's voice.

besluite.fout: With Ouma Nomsa as the subject, 'by haar' leaves the reader to work out whose hands the photo came from.
besluite.rede: Naming tannie Elsa makes the pronoun clear without adding anything, because she took out the photo in the sentences before.
'Mila het dit altyd geweet' already reads well against 'Vandag' that follows, so 'nog altyd' is only a different way of saying it in the story.

besluite.fout: 'Een reël op 'n slag' copies English 'one line at a time'.
besluite.rede: 'Reël vir reël' is the natural Afrikaans, it is shorter and plainer for a Grade 6 reader, and it means the same thing.
